distractor_reasons.A: A wholly owned subsidiary requires the maker to invest in its own overseas operation, which it is avoiding.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: When a domestic manufacturing company expands into a mature, saturated foreign market where local brands are already deeply loyal to customers, what marketing challenge will it face?

options.A: Exemption from paying shipping and customs fees
options.B: Zero competition from any domestic or foreign businesses
options.C: Customers automatically buying its unknown brand at premium prices
options.D: High promotional and advertising costs needed to build brand awareness and persuade buyers to switch

correctAnswer: High promotional and advertising costs needed to build brand awareness and persuade buyers to switch

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because breaking into established markets requires heavy marketing expenditure and competitive pricing to overcome existing brand loyalty.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because normal logistics and customs costs still apply.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because saturated markets have intense competition.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because unknown entrants rarely command premium prices without heavy brand building.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because breaking into established markets requires heavy marketing expenditure and competitive pricing to overcome existing brand loyalty.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Country P's currency depreciates steadily over three years. How can a domestic manufacturer in Country P take advantage of this currency trend?

options.A: Expand export marketing efforts abroad where its goods are now more price-competitive, and source more raw materials from domestic suppliers
options.B: Import 100% of its raw materials from abroad and stop exporting completely
options.C: Raise its domestic-currency export prices by 50% above foreign rivals
options.D: Convert all its cash reserves into foreign debt

correctAnswer: Expand export marketing efforts abroad where its goods are now more price-competitive, and source more raw materials from domestic suppliers

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because a weaker currency boosts export price competitiveness while substituting domestic inputs for costly imports protects profit margins.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because a weaker currency boosts export price competitiveness while substituting domestic inputs for costly imports protects profit margins.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because importing all inputs while abandoning exports maximises the cost penalty and misses the export opportunity.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because excessive price hikes would wipe out the export price advantage.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because foreign-currency debt becomes *more expensive* to repay when the domestic currency depreciates.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A multinational consumer goods firm has 45 subsidiaries across four continents. What organisational challenge often arises as an MNC grows across so many countries?

options.A: Communication delays, cultural misunderstandings between head office and regional managers, and diseconomies of scale
options.B: Complete inability to sell products in more than one country
options.C: Lower total sales revenue than a single local corner shop
options.D: A legal requirement that all 45 subsidiaries use the exact same language in local shops

correctAnswer: Communication delays, cultural misunderstandings between head office and regional managers, and diseconomies of scale

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because managing vast global operations across time zones and cultures increases coordination complexity and diseconomies of scale.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because managing vast global operations across time zones and cultures increases coordination complexity and diseconomies of scale.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because MNCs actively sell across dozens of countries.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because global MNCs generate vastly higher revenues than small local shops.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because local stores communicate in the local language of each market.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why might a host government require a foreign multinational company to form a joint venture with a local state or private company rather than owning 100% of the local subsidiary?

options.A: To ensure local firms share in profits, gain management expertise, and retain partial control over key national industries
options.B: To prevent the multinational from bringing any technology into the country
options.C: To guarantee that the joint venture makes a financial loss every year
options.D: To avoid collecting any tax revenue from the business

correctAnswer: To ensure local firms share in profits, gain management expertise, and retain partial control over key national industries

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because mandatory joint-venture rules help host countries capture technology transfer and retain domestic ownership stakes.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because mandatory joint-venture rules help host countries capture technology transfer and retain domestic ownership stakes.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because host governments use joint ventures specifically to *acquire* foreign technology and skills.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because both partners want the venture to be profitable.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because governments tax joint-venture profits normally.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Which statement provides the most balanced evaluation of globalisation for businesses in a developing economy?

options.A: Globalisation opens vast export markets and attracts foreign investment and technology, though weak domestic firms risk closure against powerful foreign rivals
options.B: Globalisation guarantees that every small domestic business will become a global monopoly
options.C: Globalisation destroys all economic growth and forces every country into permanent recession
options.D: Globalisation only affects agricultural farms and has zero impact on services or manufacturing

correctAnswer: Globalisation opens vast export markets and attracts foreign investment and technology, though weak domestic firms risk closure against powerful foreign rivals

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because globalisation creates major export and investment opportunities while simultaneously exposing uncompetitive local firms to intense foreign competition.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because globalisation creates major export and investment opportunities while simultaneously exposing uncompetitive local firms to intense foreign competition.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because many small local firms struggle against foreign competition rather than becoming monopolies.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because globalisation has driven rapid export-led growth in many developing economies.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because globalisation transforms manufacturing, retail, finance, and digital services.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A textile dyeing factory discharges untreated chemical wastewater into a river, forcing a downstream municipal water company to spend $300,000 per year on extra water purification. What is this $300,000 expense?

options.A: An external cost imposed on a third party by the textile factory's production
options.B: A private benefit earned by the textile factory's shareholders
options.C: An external benefit that improves river biodiversity
options.D: A fixed overhead voluntarily paid by the textile factory

correctAnswer: An external cost imposed on a third party by the textile factory's production

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because the purification cost is suffered by an uninvolved third party (the water utility and its customers) rather than paid by the polluting factory.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because the purification cost is suffered by an uninvolved third party (the water utility and its customers) rather than paid by the polluting factory.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because it is a financial cost caused by pollution, not a benefit.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because untreated wastewater harms biodiversity and creates an external cost.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because the downstream water company, not the factory, bears this cost.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A commercial forestry company plants 500,000 native trees on degraded hillside land. The company expects to earn $2 million from future sustainable timber sales (private benefit), while the new forest prevents flooding and absorbs carbon worth $900,000 to society (external benefit). What is the total social benefit?

options.A: $1.1 million
options.B: $2.0 million
options.C: $2.9 million
options.D: $0.9 million

correctAnswer: $2.9 million

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because social benefit equals private benefit ($2.0m) plus external benefit ($0.9m), which is $2.9 million.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because $1.1m subtracts external benefit from private benefit instead of adding them.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because $2.0m includes only the private benefit to the forestry firm.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because social benefit equals private benefit ($2.0m) plus external benefit ($0.9m), which is $2.9 million.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because $0.9m includes only the external benefit to society.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A chemical plant's monthly private production costs are $420,000, and its air emissions impose $85,000 per month in external respiratory health costs on nearby residents. What is the plant's monthly social cost?

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because social cost = private cost ($420,000) + external cost ($85,000) = $505,000.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because $335,000 subtracts external costs from private costs.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because $420,000 includes only private costs.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because social cost = private cost ($420,000) + external cost ($85,000) = $505,000.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because $85,000 includes only external costs.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is meant by 'sustainable development' in a business context?

options.A: Maximising short-term resource extraction even if forests and fisheries collapse permanently
options.B: Meeting the needs of today's consumers and businesses without depleting natural resources or harming ecosystems for future generations
options.C: Stopping all economic production and closing every factory permanently
options.D: Using only non-renewable fossil fuels because they are cheaper

correctAnswer: Meeting the needs of today's consumers and businesses without depleting natural resources or harming ecosystems for future generations

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because sustainable development balances current economic activity with long-term environmental stewardship and resource conservation.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because exhausting finite resources is unsustainable.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because sustainable development balances current economic activity with long-term environmental stewardship and resource conservation.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because sustainable development seeks responsible growth, not halting all human activity.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because sustainability requires transitioning toward renewable energy.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A furniture maker sources all its oak and pine from forests certified by the Forest Stewardship Council (FSC), where new trees are replanted for every tree harvested. How does this benefit the furniture maker?

options.A: It eliminates the need for carpenters and woodworking machines
options.B: It makes the timber completely free of charge
options.C: It secures a renewable long-term timber supply and allows the firm to use the recognised FSC eco-label to attract environmentally conscious buyers
options.D: It exempts the furniture maker from paying Value Added Tax

correctAnswer: It secures a renewable long-term timber supply and allows the firm to use the recognised FSC eco-label to attract environmentally conscious buyers

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because credible third-party sustainability certification prevents future resource depletion and adds marketing value.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because manufacturing furniture still requires skilled workers and equipment.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because certified sustainable timber often costs slightly more than uncertified wood.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because credible third-party sustainability certification prevents future resource depletion and adds marketing value.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because eco-certification does not waive sales taxes.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A commercial fishing fleet voluntarily uses larger-mesh fishing nets that allow young, undersized fish to escape and mature before breeding. Why is this sustainable practice commercially smart in the long run?

options.A: It increases the quantity of unsaleable juvenile fish caught today
options.B: It prevents fish stocks from collapsing, ensuring the business can continue harvesting fish profitably in future years
options.C: It eliminates fuel costs for fishing trawlers
options.D: It forces consumers to stop eating fish

correctAnswer: It prevents fish stocks from collapsing, ensuring the business can continue harvesting fish profitably in future years

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because overfishing destroys the natural capital on which the fishing business depends; preserving breeding stocks ensures long-term survival.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because larger mesh specifically reduces juvenile bycatch.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because overfishing destroys the natural capital on which the fishing business depends; preserving breeding stocks ensures long-term survival.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because fishing boats still consume marine fuel.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because sustainable catches supply fish to consumers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: An electronics manufacturer designs smartphones with modular batteries and screens that can be easily repaired with standard tools, rather than glued shut. How does this support environmental sustainability?

options.A: It forces customers to throw away their phones every six months
options.B: It extends product lifespan and reduces toxic electronic waste (e-waste) and rare-earth mining
options.C: It increases the amount of hazardous heavy metals sent to landfills
options.D: It makes smartphones impossible to recycle

correctAnswer: It extends product lifespan and reduces toxic electronic waste (e-waste) and rare-earth mining

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because designing for repairability slows resource consumption and cuts hazardous e-waste.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because easy repairs extend phone life rather than encouraging frequent replacement.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because designing for repairability slows resource consumption and cuts hazardous e-waste.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because longer device lifespans *reduce* landfill waste.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because modular parts are easier to disassemble and recycle.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A government introduces a 'landfill tax' charging businesses $120 for every tonne of solid waste sent to landfill sites, while recycled waste incurs zero tax. How is a large supermarket chain likely to respond?

options.A: Invest in in-store cardboard compactors, food-waste anaerobic digestion, and reusable delivery crates to cut landfill costs
options.B: Send twice as much mixed rubbish to landfill sites
options.C: Stop selling fresh fruit and vegetables
options.D: Burn all its plastic packaging in store car parks

correctAnswer: Invest in in-store cardboard compactors, food-waste anaerobic digestion, and reusable delivery crates to cut landfill costs

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because a steep landfill tax makes recycling and waste reduction financially profitable compared to disposal.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because a steep landfill tax makes recycling and waste reduction financially profitable compared to disposal.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because sending more waste to landfill would sharply increase tax expenses.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because fresh produce is a core supermarket category.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because open burning of plastic waste is illegal and hazardous.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: To reduce urban air pollution, a city government establishes a Low Emission Zone (LEZ) that charges older diesel delivery vans $50 per day to enter the city centre, while electric vans enter free. How does this affect a local parcel courier?

options.A: It forces couriers to deliver parcels only on foot
options.B: It lowers the operating cost of old diesel vans in the city centre
options.C: It bans all online shopping deliveries inside the city
options.D: It creates a strong financial case to lease or buy electric delivery vans for city-centre routes

correctAnswer: It creates a strong financial case to lease or buy electric delivery vans for city-centre routes

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because avoiding a $50 daily congestion/emission charge rapidly offsets the higher upfront cost of electric vans.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because electric vans and cargo bikes can legally enter free of charge.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because the $50 daily fee *increases* the cost of running older diesel vans.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because deliveries are still permitted, especially with zero-emission vehicles.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because avoiding a $50 daily congestion/emission charge rapidly offsets the higher upfront cost of electric vans.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A government sets strict legal limits on sulphur dioxide emissions from factories and imposes heavy fines plus temporary factory closure orders on firms that exceed the limit. Why do governments use regulation alongside green taxes?

options.A: Because dangerous toxic pollutants require guaranteed maximum safety limits rather than allowing rich firms to pay a tax and keep polluting
options.B: Because fines never cost businesses any money
options.C: Because green taxes are illegal under international law
options.D: Because regulations allow factories to release unlimited toxic smoke

correctAnswer: Because dangerous toxic pollutants require guaranteed maximum safety limits rather than allowing rich firms to pay a tax and keep polluting

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because command-and-control regulations set absolute ceilings on harmful emissions where public health is at immediate risk.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because command-and-control regulations set absolute ceilings on harmful emissions where public health is at immediate risk.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because heavy fines and shutdowns impose severe financial penalties.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because environmental taxes are widely used alongside regulations.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because regulations specifically *cap* emissions.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A start-up company manufactures reusable insulated stainless-steel water bottles and markets them as an eco-friendly alternative to single-use plastic bottles. Which external trend is creating rapid growth for this business?

options.A: Rising consumer awareness of ocean plastic pollution and changing social attitudes toward single-use plastics
options.B: Falling global population and declining demand for drinking water
options.C: Government bans on reusable metal bottles
options.D: A sharp drop in the price of single-use plastic waste

correctAnswer: Rising consumer awareness of ocean plastic pollution and changing social attitudes toward single-use plastics

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because environmental concern acts as a major market opportunity for innovative green products and eco-entrepreneurs.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because environmental concern acts as a major market opportunity for innovative green products and eco-entrepreneurs.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because demand for hydration products remains strong worldwide.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because governments encourage reusable bottles and restrict single-use plastics.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because consumer preference has shifted away from disposable plastic.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A detergent manufacturer launches a concentrated liquid detergent in small recyclable pouches that require 70% less plastic and 60% less lorry space to transport than bulky jugs. How does this innovation help both the environment and business profits?

options.A: It cuts carbon emissions and plastic waste while simultaneously lowering packaging material and haulage costs per wash
options.B: It increases packaging material costs and transport fuel bills
options.C: It forces customers to buy three times more water in heavy plastic bottles
options.D: It reduces supermarket shelf space efficiency

correctAnswer: It cuts carbon emissions and plastic waste while simultaneously lowering packaging material and haulage costs per wash

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because lightweight concentrated packaging is a classic 'eco-efficiency' win-win that lowers unit costs and environmental footprint.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because lightweight concentrated packaging is a classic 'eco-efficiency' win-win that lowers unit costs and environmental footprint.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because using 70% less plastic and 60% less lorry space *reduces* costs.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because concentrated detergent removes excess water from the packaging.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because compact pouches take up *less* shelf space per wash.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why might a small family-owned bakery struggle more than a large multinational food corporation to comply with complex new environmental reporting and carbon-auditing laws?

options.A: The small bakery lacks specialist sustainability staff and cannot spread fixed compliance and auditing fees over millions of units
options.B: Small bakeries are legally required to pay double the carbon tax rate of multinationals
options.C: Multinational corporations are exempt from all environmental laws
options.D: Small bakeries never use electricity or ovens

correctAnswer: The small bakery lacks specialist sustainability staff and cannot spread fixed compliance and auditing fees over millions of units

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because regulatory compliance carries fixed administrative costs that fall disproportionately heavily on small businesses.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because regulatory compliance carries fixed administrative costs that fall disproportionately heavily on small businesses.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because tax rates are not doubled for small firms.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because MNCs face strict environmental reporting mandates.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because bakeries use ovens and energy.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A water-bottling company extracts millions of litres of groundwater daily from a rural aquifer, causing local farmers' irrigation wells to run dry during summer. Which conflict between stakeholder groups does this illustrate?

options.A: The company's profit and production goals conflicting with the local community's and farmers' access to shared natural resources
options.B: Local farmers demanding the bottling company pump even more water
options.C: Shareholders asking the company to stop selling bottled water
options.D: Complete harmony between industrial water extraction and local agriculture

correctAnswer: The company's profit and production goals conflicting with the local community's and farmers' access to shared natural resources

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because over-exploiting a common natural resource imposes severe external costs on neighbouring agricultural businesses and residents.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because over-exploiting a common natural resource imposes severe external costs on neighbouring agricultural businesses and residents.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because local farmers suffer when their wells dry up.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because shareholders seek profitable output unless stopped by regulation or protests.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because depleting the shared aquifer creates direct conflict.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A clothing retailer installs rooftop solar panels that cut carbon emissions and reduce electricity bills. Which argument best supports the decision in terms of sustainable development?

options.A: It reduces environmental impact while also lowering long-term costs
options.B: It increases the firm's dependence on fossil fuels
options.C: It guarantees an immediate profit within the first month
options.D: It removes all of the firm's legal responsibilities

correctAnswer: It reduces environmental impact while also lowering long-term costs

explanation.correct_reason: Sustainable development balances environmental protection with economic benefit, and cheaper clean energy achieves both.

distractor_reasons.B: Solar power reduces reliance on fossil fuels, not increases it.
distractor_reasons.C: An installation may take years to pay for itself, so immediate profit in the first month is not guaranteed.
distractor_reasons.D: Installing panels does not release the firm from other legal duties, such as safety and employment law.
distractor_reasons.A: Sustainable development balances environmental protection with economic benefit, and cheaper clean energy achieves both.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A supermarket chain places 'Carbon Footprint Score' labels (from A to E) on all food products so shoppers can see the greenhouse gas impact of their groceries. How is this likely to influence food suppliers?

options.A: Suppliers will compete to reduce farming and packaging emissions to earn an 'A' rating and avoid losing eco-conscious shoppers
options.B: Suppliers will deliberately increase emissions to get an 'E' rating
options.C: Shoppers will stop buying any food with an 'A' rating
options.D: Supermarkets will stop selling fresh vegetables

correctAnswer: Suppliers will compete to reduce farming and packaging emissions to earn an 'A' rating and avoid losing eco-conscious shoppers

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because transparent environmental labelling nudges consumer choice and creates competitive pressure across the supply chain.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because transparent environmental labelling nudges consumer choice and creates competitive pressure across the supply chain.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because poor environmental ratings deter eco-conscious buyers.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because 'A' represents the lowest, most desirable carbon footprint.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because vegetables typically score very well ('A') on carbon footprint.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why do some budget airlines resist investing immediately in Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) even though it cuts lifecycle carbon emissions by up to 80%?

options.A: Conventional jet fuel produces zero carbon emissions
options.B: Sustainable Aviation Fuel is banned by international aviation authorities
options.C: Sustainable Aviation Fuel currently costs two to four times more than conventional jet fuel, which would raise ticket prices and reduce price competitiveness
options.D: Airlines do not spend any money on fuel

correctAnswer: Sustainable Aviation Fuel currently costs two to four times more than conventional jet fuel, which would raise ticket prices and reduce price competitiveness

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because high short-term input costs create a commercial dilemma in price-competitive industries unless matched by mandates or subsidies.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because conventional kerosene jet fuel is a major source of CO2 emissions.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because SAF is approved and actively blended into commercial flights.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because high short-term input costs create a commercial dilemma in price-competitive industries unless matched by mandates or subsidies.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because fuel is one of an airline's largest operating expenses.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A city council builds a new underground metro line. Construction causes two years of noise and dust for shopkeepers (external cost), but once open, it reduces traffic jams, cuts air pollution, and brings thousands of extra shoppers to high-street stores (external benefit). How should the council evaluate this project?

options.A: Use cost-benefit analysis to compare total long-term social benefits against total social costs, rather than looking only at short-term disruption
options.B: Cancel the project because any temporary construction dust is always unacceptable
options.C: Ignore all environmental and community impacts completely
options.D: Charge shopkeepers a fine for having fewer customers during construction

correctAnswer: Use cost-benefit analysis to compare total long-term social benefits against total social costs, rather than looking only at short-term disruption

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because public infrastructure decisions weigh temporary private/external construction costs against decades of social and environmental benefits.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because public infrastructure decisions weigh temporary private/external construction costs against decades of social and environmental benefits.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because long-term social benefits often far outweigh temporary construction disruption.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because public bodies must assess social and environmental externalities.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because councils often provide business-rate relief rather than fines during roadworks.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A paper manufacturer shifts from bleaching office paper with chlorine gas (which produces toxic dioxins) to using an oxygen-based bleaching process after installing new filtration equipment. What type of environmental business response is this?

options.A: Bribing environmental inspectors
options.B: Relocating pollution to another country
options.C: Greenwashing without changing manufacturing processes
options.D: Investing in cleaner production technology to prevent pollution at source

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A hotel chain removes miniature single-use plastic shampoo bottles from all 10,000 guest rooms and installs refillable wall-mounted dispensers. Which two outcomes does this achieve?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A national government sets a legally binding target for all new passenger cars sold after 2035 to be zero-emission vehicles. How does this long-term environmental policy affect traditional petrol-engine carmakers today?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Under a 'cap-and-trade' emissions trading scheme, heavy industries are given a limited number of carbon permits; firms that cut emissions below their allowance can sell spare permits to higher-emitting firms. Why is this system used?

options.B: It allows factories to release unlimited greenhouse gases for free

options.D: It puts a market price on carbon emissions and financially rewards businesses that innovate to cut pollution fastest

correctAnswer: It puts a market price on carbon emissions and financially rewards businesses that innovate to cut pollution fastest

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because cap-and-trade caps total industry emissions while creating a financial reward (selling surplus permits) for green efficiency.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because cap-and-trade targets major industrial emitters such as power stations and steelworks.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because total permits are strictly capped and excess emitters must buy permits.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because firms can continue operating by cutting emissions or purchasing permits.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because cap-and-trade caps total industry emissions while creating a financial reward (selling surplus permits) for green efficiency.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A ski resort operating at low altitude experiences shorter winter snow seasons due to rising global temperatures. How might the business adapt strategically to this environmental change?

correctAnswer: Diversify into year-round mountain biking, hiking, and eco-wellness retreats so it is not dependent solely on winter snow

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because diversifying into summer and autumn outdoor tourism protects revenue against climate-driven declines in winter snowfall.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because diversifying into summer and autumn outdoor tourism protects revenue against climate-driven declines in winter snowfall.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because huge price hikes for shorter snow seasons would drive skiers away.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because building ski lifts where snow is unreliable wastes capital.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because high-quality facilities are essential to attract year-round guests.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A coffee roaster offers a 20% discount to customers who bring refillable containers to its stores and composts 100% of its coffee chaff waste with local urban farms. Beyond environmental benefits, what marketing advantage does this create?

options.A: Higher packaging waste disposal bills

distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because visible, authentic circular-economy initiatives build community goodwill and repeat customer visits.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Which statement best evaluates whether becoming environmentally sustainable always reduces a business's profit?

correctAnswer: Although green technologies and sustainable materials often require high upfront investment, they frequently increase long-term profit through lower energy/waste bills, stronger brand loyalty, and avoided green taxes

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because a balanced evaluation distinguishes between short-term capital/input costs and long-term cost savings, tax avoidance, and revenue growth.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because many sustainable firms outperform rivals in profitability and resilience.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because renewable energy, eco-packaging, and certified inputs often cost more initially.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: In Country A, the statutory minimum wage is $8.00 per hour, which is not enough for a family to afford basic housing and food. A clothing retailer voluntarily pays all store and warehouse staff a 'Real Living Wage' of $12.50 per hour. What does this illustrate?

options.A: Acting ethically by going beyond minimum legal requirements to ensure fair living standards for employees

options.C: Predatory pricing to eliminate rival clothing retailers
options.D: Profit repatriation to foreign shareholders

correctAnswer: Acting ethically by going beyond minimum legal requirements to ensure fair living standards for employees

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A toy company uses colourful cartoon characters in online mobile games to trick young children into making accidental in-app purchases using their parents' credit cards without clear warnings. Why is this practice widely condemned as unethical?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A profitable multinational technology company uses complex accounting loopholes to route all its profits through a zero-tax island, paying almost zero corporation tax in the countries where it earns billions in sales. Why do critics view this as unethical even if technically legal?

options.A: Because customers prefer companies that avoid paying public taxes

distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because avoiding tax increases retained profits, which is why firms do it.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because aggressive tax avoidance highlights the gap between strict legality and moral fairness toward host societies.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A coffee roaster joins the Fairtrade Foundation, guaranteeing smallholder coffee farmers a fair minimum price above production costs plus an extra social premium for local schools and clinics. What is the main trade-off for the coffee roaster?

options.A: Loss of all supermarket retail shelf space

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A pharmaceutical company discovers during internal testing that a popular painkiller causes rare heart side effects, even though regulators have not yet requested a recall. What is the ethical action for the company's directors?

distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because falsifying or destroying safety data is illegal and immoral.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because dumping unsafe products in developing nations is a severe ethical violation.

question: A construction company wins a major government highway contract, and it later emerges that the company's sales director paid $200,000 in secret bribes to government procurement officials. What are two likely consequences for the company?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity

options.C: Making it impossible to contact successful candidates for interviews

correctAnswer: Preventing unconscious bias based on gender, ethnicity, age, or social background so hiring is based strictly on skills and merit

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because anonymising personal identifiers promotes genuine equal opportunity and fair merit-based selection.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because anonymising personal identifiers promotes genuine equal opportunity and fair merit-based selection.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because removing addresses eliminates postcode/wealth bias.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because HR retains contact details separately to invite shortlisted candidates.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because blind recruitment ensures fair selection, not lower wages.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A fast-food restaurant advertises a 'Giant Double Steak Burger' using professional food styling where the burger looks twice as large as the actual sandwich served to customers. Why is this an ethical and legal issue?

options.B: Customers always enjoy receiving smaller portions than advertised
options.C: Misleading advertising deceives consumers, breaches advertising standards codes, and damages customer trust
options.D: Smaller burgers increase customer satisfaction scores

correctAnswer: Misleading advertising deceives consumers, breaches advertising standards codes, and damages customer trust

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because deceptive product representation violates ethical marketing principles and consumer protection rules.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because accurate food photography is completely legal.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because feeling misled frustrates customers and reduces repeat visits.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because deceptive product representation violates ethical marketing principles and consumer protection rules.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because unmet expectations lower customer satisfaction.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A company's Board of Directors links 25% of senior executives' annual bonuses to achieving verified targets for workplace safety, staff retention, and carbon reduction alongside financial profit. Why is this governance structure effective?

options.A: It guarantees that the company will never make any profit
options.B: It aligns managers' personal financial incentives with long-term ethical and sustainable performance rather than short-term profit alone
options.C: It encourages managers to ignore workplace safety
options.D: It eliminates the need for employees to follow safety rules

correctAnswer: It aligns managers' personal financial incentives with long-term ethical and sustainable performance rather than short-term profit alone

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because tying executive pay to non-financial ethical metrics ensures leaders treat ethics as a core strategic priority.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because 75% of the bonus remains tied to financial performance and sustainable firms remain profitable.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because tying executive pay to non-financial ethical metrics ensures leaders treat ethics as a core strategic priority.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because linking bonuses to safety motivates managers to *improve* safety.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because all workers and managers must follow safety procedures.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A global coffee chain closes all 8,000 of its stores for one afternoon—losing millions of dollars in daily sales—to conduct mandatory anti-bias and inclusive customer service training for all 175,000 employees after an incident in one store. Why did management make this costly decision?

options.A: To demonstrate genuine commitment to ethical values, repair brand reputation, and prevent future discrimination across the chain
options.B: Because the company wanted to permanently go out of business
options.C: Because coffee beans had become illegal to sell
options.D: To avoid paying employees their afternoon wages

correctAnswer: To demonstrate genuine commitment to ethical values, repair brand reputation, and prevent future discrimination across the chain

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because decisive, visible investment in staff values protects long-term brand equity even at high short-term revenue cost.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because decisive, visible investment in staff values protects long-term brand equity even at high short-term revenue cost.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because the closure was for a single afternoon to strengthen the brand's future.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because coffee sales resumed immediately after training.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because staff were paid to attend the mandatory training session.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: How can unethical business practices in a single company eventually lead to stricter government laws affecting the entire industry?

options.A: Governments reward unethical scandals by removing all industry regulations
options.B: Public scandals and media outrage force governments to pass new regulations that impose higher compliance costs on all firms in the sector
options.C: Unethical scandals automatically reduce compliance costs for competitors
options.D: Lawmakers ignore all major corporate scandals

correctAnswer: Public scandals and media outrage force governments to pass new regulations that impose higher compliance costs on all firms in the sector

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because when businesses fail to self-regulate ethically, governments step in with statutory laws to protect stakeholders.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because scandals prompt *tighter*, not looser, regulation.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because when businesses fail to self-regulate ethically, governments step in with statutory laws to protect stakeholders.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because new statutory rules raise compliance costs across the industry.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because public outcry pressures politicians to legislate.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is the primary difference between a pressure group and a political party?

options.A: A pressure group runs candidates to become prime minister and run the whole country
options.B: A pressure group seeks to influence specific business practices or government policies on particular issues without seeking to form the government itself
options.C: A pressure group is a profit-making public limited company
options.D: A pressure group has the legal authority to pass criminal laws

correctAnswer: A pressure group seeks to influence specific business practices or government policies on particular issues without seeking to form the government itself

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because pressure groups focus on advocating specific causes (environmental, consumer, ethical) rather than winning general elections to govern.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because contesting elections to form a government is the role of a political party.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because pressure groups focus on advocating specific causes (environmental, consumer, ethical) rather than winning general elections to govern.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because pressure groups are non-profit advocacy organisations.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because only parliaments/governments pass laws; pressure groups lobby lawmakers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: An animal welfare pressure group launches a viral social media video campaign exposing cramped cage conditions at a large egg producer, using a hashtag that trends nationally for two weeks. How does social media increase pressure group power?

options.A: It eliminates the egg producer's feed and electricity expenses
options.B: It legally forces supermarkets to close down within 24 hours
options.C: It prevents consumers from reading any news about the company
options.D: It allows pressure groups to reach millions of consumers instantly at very low cost, threatening rapid brand damage

correctAnswer: It allows pressure groups to reach millions of consumers instantly at very low cost, threatening rapid brand damage

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because viral digital campaigns amplify negative publicity at negligible cost, putting immediate reputational pressure on consumer brands.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because operating expenses are unaffected by social media hashtags.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because social media generates reputational pressure, not automatic legal closure.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because viral posts *spread* information widely rather than hiding it.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because viral digital campaigns amplify negative publicity at negligible cost, putting immediate reputational pressure on consumer brands.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: During a consumer boycott organised by an environmental pressure group against a bottled-water brand, what is the immediate financial risk to the targeted business?

options.A: A government subsidy compensating the firm for lost sales
options.B: An immediate 50% increase in profit margins
options.C: Falling sales revenue and excess unsold inventory while fixed factory and marketing overheads continue
options.D: Automatic elimination of all fixed overhead costs

correctAnswer: Falling sales revenue and excess unsold inventory while fixed factory and marketing overheads continue

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because boycotts reduce cash inflows from sales while fixed costs still have to be paid, squeezing profits and cash flow.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because governments do not compensate firms for consumer boycotts.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because lower sales volumes reduce rather than increase profits.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because boycotts reduce cash inflows from sales while fixed costs still have to be paid, squeezing profits and cash flow.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because rent, salaries, and loan interest remain payable.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A road-safety pressure group presents detailed crash statistics to transport ministers, persuading the government to make automatic emergency braking mandatory in all new cars. How has this pressure group affected car manufacturers?

options.A: Indirectly, by successfully lobbying the government to introduce new legal safety standards that manufacturers must obey
options.B: Directly, by buying 51% of shares in every car manufacturer
options.C: By banning all citizens from owning cars
options.D: By lowering car manufacturing costs to zero

correctAnswer: Indirectly, by successfully lobbying the government to introduce new legal safety standards that manufacturers must obey

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because pressure groups frequently influence business operations indirectly by convincing governments to legislate.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because pressure groups frequently influence business operations indirectly by convincing governments to legislate.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because the group used political lobbying, not a corporate takeover.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because cars remain legal with enhanced safety equipment.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adding mandatory safety sensors increases unit production costs.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Why is a pressure group campaign against a well-known high-street fashion retailer much more likely to succeed than a campaign against an anonymous mining company that sells raw iron ore only to steel mills?

options.A: The fashion retailer relies directly on consumer brand image and faces thousands of retail competitors, whereas the mining firm has no direct retail shoppers to boycott it
options.B: Mining companies are legally immune from all environmental laws
options.C: Fashion retailers never care about sales revenue
options.D: Iron ore mining has zero impact on the environment

correctAnswer: The fashion retailer relies directly on consumer brand image and faces thousands of retail competitors, whereas the mining firm has no direct retail shoppers to boycott it

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because business-to-consumer (B2C) brands are highly sensitive to public reputation and consumer boycotts, unlike behind-the-scenes B2B commodity suppliers.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because business-to-consumer (B2C) brands are highly sensitive to public reputation and consumer boycotts, unlike behind-the-scenes B2B commodity suppliers.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because mining companies must obey environmental regulations.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because fashion retailers depend heavily on sales and brand appeal.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because mining has major environmental impacts, making it a target for lobbying rather than retail boycotts.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A disability rights pressure group audits the websites of 20 major online supermarkets and publishes a league table ranking them from most accessible to least accessible for blind and visually impaired shoppers. Why is publishing a league table effective?

options.A: Low-ranked supermarkets suffer public embarrassment and risk losing disabled shoppers and their families to higher-ranked rivals
options.B: League tables legally shut down the bottom ten supermarkets
options.C: Supermarkets prefer finishing at the bottom of public customer-service rankings
options.D: Blind shoppers never buy groceries online

correctAnswer: Low-ranked supermarkets suffer public embarrassment and risk losing disabled shoppers and their families to higher-ranked rivals

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because comparative public scorecards create peer competition and reputational pressure for laggards to improve.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because comparative public scorecards create peer competition and reputational pressure for laggards to improve.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because NGO league tables create reputational pressure, not legal closures.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because retailers strive to avoid negative public rankings.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because accessible online grocery shopping is hugely valuable for visually impaired customers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A local residents' pressure group opposes a delivery depot operating heavy lorries through narrow residential streets at 3:00 AM. How can the depot manager constructively resolve the conflict?

options.A: Meet with resident representatives, restrict heavy lorry movements to daytime hours, and reroute vehicles onto the main ring road
options.B: Increase 3:00 AM lorry deliveries through the residential streets
options.C: Refuse to speak to residents and ignore noise complaints
options.D: Close the entire business permanently without exploring route changes

correctAnswer: Meet with resident representatives, restrict heavy lorry movements to daytime hours, and reroute vehicles onto the main ring road

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because constructive stakeholder dialogue and practical operational adjustments resolve local friction without sacrificing the business.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because constructive stakeholder dialogue and practical operational adjustments resolve local friction without sacrificing the business.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because worsening the noise nuisance would provoke council enforcement and protests.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because ignoring valid community complaints risks local council night-time bans.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adjusting delivery times and routes solves the problem without closing the depot.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A pressure group calls for a boycott of the only pharmaceutical manufacturer producing a life-saving insulin medicine over high prices. Why will diabetic patients not participate in a consumer boycott?

options.A: Diabetic patients do not care about medicine prices
options.B: Insulin is a vital life-saving necessity with no immediate substitute, so patients must keep buying it to survive
options.C: Pharmaceutical companies give away all medicines for free
options.D: Pressure groups are legally banned from criticising drug prices

correctAnswer: Insulin is a vital life-saving necessity with no immediate substitute, so patients must keep buying it to survive

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because boycotts fail when the product is an essential necessity lacking close substitutes; pressure groups must instead lobby health regulators.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because patients care deeply about high prices, which is why advocates lobby governments for price caps.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because boycotts fail when the product is an essential necessity lacking close substitutes; pressure groups must instead lobby health regulators.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because commercial drugmakers charge prices to recover R&D and earn profits.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because advocacy groups regularly campaign on medicine affordability.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A coalition of 40 environmental and consumer pressure groups forms a joint campaign demanding a ban on toxic 'forever chemicals' (PFAS) in non-stick frying pans. Why is a coalition more effective than a single small pressure group?

options.A: Pooling funds, scientific researchers, media contacts, and millions of members creates far stronger political and commercial leverage
options.B: Coalitions are legally allowed to pass laws without Parliament
options.C: Coalitions eliminate all manufacturing costs for cookware firms
options.D: Single small pressure groups always have more money than 40 groups combined

correctAnswer: Pooling funds, scientific researchers, media contacts, and millions of members creates far stronger political and commercial leverage

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because uniting multiple organisations amplifies credibility, financial backing, and voter/consumer reach.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because uniting multiple organisations amplifies credibility, financial backing, and voter/consumer reach.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because coalitions still lobby lawmakers rather than passing laws themselves.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because switching away from PFAS requires R&D into alternative coatings.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because combining 40 organisations pools vastly greater resources.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: After pressure groups campaign against palm oil linked to rainforest deforestation, a biscuit manufacturer switches to 100% certified sustainable palm oil (RSPO) and partners with the conservation group to audit its plantations. unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A local heritage pressure group campaigns to stop a supermarket chain from demolishing a historic 19th-century Victorian train station to build a car park. unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A small fringe group with no scientific evidence claims on a blog that 5G mobile phone masts cause illness and demands that telecom companies dismantle all masts. Why will telecom companies ignore the demand to remove masts while publishing clear scientific safety facts?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity

distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because central banks set monetary policy.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A consumer pressure group publishes test results showing that a popular brand of children's car seats fails high-speed side-impact safety tests, even though it passed older minimum legal tests. Why will the manufacturer recall and redesign the seat immediately?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A farming trade association (a business pressure group) lobbies the government to block imports of cheap foreign beef produced with growth hormones banned domestically. What is the trade association trying to achieve?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: When evaluating the impact of a pressure group's boycott on a multinational business, why is it important to consider whether the boycott is local or international?

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A pressure group campaigns against a major bank's plans to close its last remaining rural bank branches, arguing that elderly residents and small rural shops will be unable to deposit cash. How could the bank respond to satisfy both cost-cutting goals and the pressure group?

options.C: Keep every large, loss-making branch open 24 hours a day seven days a week
options.D: Charge rural elderly customers $50 every time they check their balance

correctAnswer: Share banking hubs with other banks in rural post offices or run mobile banking vans on scheduled days rather than leaving villages with zero service

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because shared banking hubs and mobile vans cut fixed branch overheads while preserving essential community access and goodwill.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because shared banking hubs and mobile vans cut fixed branch overheads while preserving essential community access and goodwill.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because total abandonment fuels fierce public and political backlash.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because keeping underused branches open 24/7 is financially unsustainable.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because punitive fees would outrage regulators and customers.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: How do pressure groups act as an 'early warning system' for forward-thinking business managers?

options.A: They highlight emerging social, ethical, and environmental concerns early, giving proactive firms time to adapt before laws change or scandals erupt
options.B: They secretly manage the business's daily payroll and accounting
options.C: They guarantee that consumer tastes will never change
options.D: They prevent governments from ever passing new regulations

correctAnswer: They highlight emerging social, ethical, and environmental concerns early, giving proactive firms time to adapt before laws change or scandals erupt

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because pressure group campaigns often signal future shifts in consumer expectations and legislation, enabling early movers to gain a competitive edge.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because pressure group campaigns often signal future shifts in consumer expectations and legislation, enabling early movers to gain a competitive edge.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because pressure groups are external bodies, not internal administrators.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because pressure groups actively drive changes in consumer attitudes.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because pressure groups frequently campaign *for* new regulations.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: A multinational food manufacturer faces sustained pressure group campaigns over plastic packaging, high sugar content, and supply-chain deforestation. Which comprehensive strategic response is most effective for long-term business survival?

options.A: Ignore all pressure groups, consumers, and lawmakers until sales collapse
options.B: Spend millions on misleading green adverts without changing any ingredients or packaging
options.C: Set measurable, independently verified targets for recyclable packaging, healthier product reformulation, and deforestation-free sourcing, and report progress transparently
options.D: Close the company and return all assets to the government

correctAnswer: Set measurable, independently verified targets for recyclable packaging, healthier product reformulation, and deforestation-free sourcing, and report progress transparently

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because genuine operational reform backed by transparent verification addresses the root causes of external pressure and secures long-term competitiveness.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because ignoring major external shifts in consumer and regulatory expectations leads to long-term decline.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because greenwashing backfires severely when exposed by pressure groups and regulators.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because genuine operational reform backed by transparent verification addresses the root causes of external pressure and secures long-term competitiveness.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because adapting products and supply chains allows the business to thrive profitably.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is meant by the term Gross Domestic Product (GDP)?

options.A: The percentage increase in the average price level of goods and services over twelve months.
options.B: The total amount of tax revenue collected by a government from private businesses each year.
options.C: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given time period.
options.D: The difference between the value of a country's exports and the value of its imports.

correctAnswer: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country in a given time period.

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total value of output of goods and services produced inside an economy over a specific period, usually a year.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because a sustained rise in average prices defines inflation, not GDP.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because this describes government tax receipts rather than national economic output.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total value of output of goods and services produced inside an economy over a specific period, usually a year.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because exports minus imports measures the trade balance on the balance of payments.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is meant by the economic term inflation?

options.A: A period of two consecutive quarters of falling national output.
options.B: A sustained increase in the average price level of goods and services in an economy over time.
options.C: An increase in the external value of a country's currency against foreign currencies.
options.D: A fall in the total number of people actively seeking paid employment.

correctAnswer: A sustained increase in the average price level of goods and services in an economy over time.

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because inflation is defined as a persistent rise in general prices across an economy, which reduces the purchasing power of money.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because two consecutive quarters of falling GDP defines an economic recession.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because inflation is defined as a persistent rise in general prices across an economy, which reduces the purchasing power of money.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because a rise in a currency's value defines currency appreciation.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because a fall in job seekers relates to falling unemployment or a shrinking labour force.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Which statement accurately defines unemployment?

options.A: All citizens in a country who are retired, in full-time school, or unable to work.
options.B: Workers who are employed on part-time contracts rather than full-time contracts.
options.C: People who are willing and able to work at current wage rates but cannot find a job.
options.D: Employees who voluntarily leave one job and start another job on the same day.

correctAnswer: People who are willing and able to work at current wage rates but cannot find a job.

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because unemployment includes individuals of working age who are actively seeking work and available to start, yet are without paid employment.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because retirees and full-time students are economically inactive rather than unemployed.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because part-time workers are classified as employed.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because unemployment includes individuals of working age who are actively seeking work and available to start, yet are without paid employment.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because moving immediately into another job involves no period of unemployment.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What does the balance of payments record for a country?

options.A: The total value of wages paid to public sector employees each year.
options.B: The difference between government tax revenue and government expenditure.
options.C: The total amount of money borrowed by private businesses from commercial banks.
options.D: The financial record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

correctAnswer: The financial record of all economic transactions between residents of a country and the rest of the world.

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because the balance of payments records all international inflows and outflows of money, including exports and imports of goods and services.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because public sector wages are part of government expenditure, not international transactions.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because government revenue minus spending is the fiscal budget balance.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because domestic bank lending is recorded in domestic monetary statistics.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because the balance of payments records all international inflows and outflows of money, including exports and imports of goods and services.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Which characteristics describe the growth stage of the business cycle?

options.A: Rising GDP, falling unemployment, increasing consumer spending, and higher business investment.
options.B: Falling GDP, rising business bankruptcies, and high spare factory capacity.
options.C: Negative economic growth, collapsing business confidence, and rising redundancies.
options.D: Minimum levels of national output, severe deflation, and mass long-term unemployment.

correctAnswer: Rising GDP, falling unemployment, increasing consumer spending, and higher business investment.

explanation.correct_reason: Option A is correct because the growth stage is marked by expanding national output (GDP), rising employment, higher incomes, and growing business optimism.

distractor_reasons.A: Option A is correct because the growth stage is marked by expanding national output (GDP), rising employment, higher incomes, and growing business optimism.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because falling GDP and rising bankruptcies characterise a recession or slump.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because negative GDP growth and rising redundancies occur during a recession.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because the trough of lowest output and mass unemployment defines a slump.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Which feature is most closely associated with the boom stage of the business cycle?

options.A: Widespread spare production capacity and falling prices across most industries.
options.B: Very high consumer demand, low unemployment, skill shortages, and rising inflationary pressure.
options.C: Two consecutive quarters of declining Gross Domestic Product.
options.D: High levels of cyclical unemployment and falling business profits.

correctAnswer: Very high consumer demand, low unemployment, skill shortages, and rising inflationary pressure.

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because an economic boom represents the peak of the business cycle, where rapid spending creates labour shortages, capacity bottlenecks, and rising inflation.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because spare capacity and falling prices occur during a slump.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because an economic boom represents the peak of the business cycle, where rapid spending creates labour shortages, capacity bottlenecks, and rising inflation.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because two quarters of falling GDP defines a recession.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because high cyclical unemployment occurs in recessions and slumps, not booms.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: How is an economic recession formally defined?

options.A: A period when the annual inflation rate rises above 5%.
options.B: A period when a country's exports exceed its imports.
options.C: A period of negative economic growth where real GDP falls for two or more consecutive quarters.
options.D: A period when commercial banks lower interest rates to stimulate borrowing.

correctAnswer: A period of negative economic growth where real GDP falls for two or more consecutive quarters.

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because economists define a recession as at least two successive quarters (six months) of contracting real GDP.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because rising prices define inflation, which is distinct from falling national output.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because exports exceeding imports describes a trade surplus.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because economists define a recession as at least two successive quarters (six months) of contracting real GDP.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because cutting interest rates is a policy response to a downturn, not the definition of a recession.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: Which stage of the business cycle represents a prolonged and severe downturn with very high unemployment and low consumer confidence?

options.A: Boom
options.B: Recovery
options.C: Expansion
options.D: Slump

correctAnswer: Slump

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because a slump is the lowest trough of the business cycle, characterised by deep, prolonged contraction, business failures, and high unemployment.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because a boom is the peak of rapid growth and low unemployment.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because recovery occurs when GDP begins rising again after a downturn.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because expansion refers to sustained upward growth in GDP.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because a slump is the lowest trough of the business cycle, characterised by deep, prolonged contraction, business failures, and high unemployment.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is meant by fiscal policy?

options.A: The setting of exchange rates by commercial currency traders.
options.B: The control of interest rates and the money supply by a country's central bank.
options.C: The imposition of import quotas and tariffs to restrict foreign competition.
options.D: The use of government taxation and public expenditure to influence aggregate demand and economic activity.

correctAnswer: The use of government taxation and public expenditure to influence aggregate demand and economic activity.

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because fiscal policy involves government decisions on direct and indirect tax rates alongside government spending levels.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because floating exchange rates are determined by market supply and demand.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because changing interest rates and the money supply defines monetary policy.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because tariffs and quotas are trade protectionist measures.
distractor_reasons.D: Option D is correct because fiscal policy involves government decisions on direct and indirect tax rates alongside government spending levels.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is meant by monetary policy?

options.A: Government changes to income tax and corporation tax rates.
options.B: Central bank decisions regarding interest rates and the supply of money in the economy.
options.C: Government spending on state schools, hospitals, and highways.
options.D: Legal regulations setting minimum environmental standards for factories.

correctAnswer: Central bank decisions regarding interest rates and the supply of money in the economy.

explanation.correct_reason: Option B is correct because monetary policy regulates the cost of borrowing (interest rates) and money supply to control inflation and economic activity.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because changing tax rates is an instrument of fiscal policy.
distractor_reasons.B: Option B is correct because monetary policy regulates the cost of borrowing (interest rates) and money supply to control inflation and economic activity.
distractor_reasons.C: Incorrect because public infrastructure and social spending are components of fiscal policy.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because environmental rules are regulatory policies rather than monetary policy.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is the main aim of government supply-side policies?

options.A: To reduce consumer spending by raising Value Added Tax on all goods.
options.B: To increase import tariffs on foreign raw materials.
options.C: To improve the productive efficiency, competitiveness, and long-term output capacity of the economy.
options.D: To raise central bank interest rates to discourage business investment.

correctAnswer: To improve the productive efficiency, competitiveness, and long-term output capacity of the economy.

explanation.correct_reason: Option C is correct because supply-side policies (such as education, training, deregulation, and infrastructure investment) enhance productivity and long-run economic growth.

distractor_reasons.A: Incorrect because raising VAT is a contractionary fiscal policy aimed at reducing demand.
distractor_reasons.B: Incorrect because import tariffs are protectionist barriers rather than supply-side efficiency reforms.
distractor_reasons.C: Option C is correct because supply-side policies (such as education, training, deregulation, and infrastructure investment) enhance productivity and long-run economic growth.
distractor_reasons.D: Incorrect because raising interest rates is contractionary monetary policy.

unit: Unit 6: External influences on business activity
question: What is a direct tax?

options.A: A tax added onto the selling price of goods and services when they are purchased.
options.B: A customs duty charged only on goods imported from abroad.
options.C: A fee paid by consumers to obtain a passport or driving licence.
options.D: A tax levied directly on the income of individuals or the profits of businesses.

correctAnswer: A tax levied directly on the income of individuals or the profits of businesses.

explanation.correct_reason: Option D is correct because direct taxes (such as income tax and corporation tax) are paid directly by individuals or companies to the government based on earnings or profits.
